# Giv (گیو) in the Shahnameh

Giv is one of the most prominent Iranian heroes (pahlavans) in Ferdowsi's *Shahnameh* ("Book of Kings"), the Persian national epic completed around 1010 CE. He is a major figure throughout the heroic and legendary portions of the epic.

## Family and Lineage

- **Father**: Gudarz (Godarz), the patriarch of one of Iran's greatest noble houses, the Gudarzian clan
- **Grandfather**: Keshvad (Kashvad), a hero of earlier generations
- **Wife**: Banu Goshasp (in some traditions) or more famously, he marries **Farangis**, the daughter of Afrasiyab and widow of Siyavash, though more accurately he serves as her protector
- **Son**: **Bizhan** (Bijan), the hero of the famous romance "Bizhan and Manizheh"
- He is part of an enormous extended family — Gudarz reportedly had 78 sons, many of whom died at the Battle of the Eleven Champions

## Major Exploits

### The Quest for Kay Khosrow
Giv's most celebrated achievement is his seven-year search for **Kay Khosrow**, the son of the murdered prince Siyavash, in the lands of Turan. He wandered alone through hostile territory, enduring tremendous hardship, before finding the young prince. He then helped Kay Khosrow and his mother Farangis escape across the Jihun (Oxus) River back to Iran, with the Turanian army in pursuit. This act made him a kingmaker, as Kay Khosrow became one of Iran's greatest kings.

### Wars Against Turan
Giv fought in virtually every major Iranian campaign against Afrasiyab and the Turanians:
- He participated in the wars under Kay Kavus
- He fought in the campaigns to avenge Siyavash
- He was present at the **Battle of the Twelve Rukhs** (Davazdah Rukh), where he defeated his Turanian opponent in single combat
- He helped capture and bring Afrasiyab to justice

### The Rescue of Bizhan
When his son Bizhan was imprisoned in a pit by Afrasiyab, Giv was overcome with grief. He played a key role in convincing Kay Khosrow to send Rostam to rescue Bizhan from Turan.

## Character and Significance

- **Loyalty**: Giv epitomizes loyalty to the Iranian crown and to the legitimate kingship
- **Endurance**: His seven-year solitary quest demonstrates extraordinary perseverance
- **Warrior prowess**: He is consistently described among the top-tier Iranian champions, second perhaps only to Rostam, Tus, and a few others
- **Statesman**: He often serves as a counselor and emissary, not merely a warrior

## Symbolic Importance

Giv represents the ideal vassal-hero in the Shahnameh — fiercely devoted, willing to suffer alone for the greater good of Iran, and a bridge between generations of heroes. His role in restoring the rightful king (Kay Khosrow) places him among the most pivotal figures in the epic's dynastic narrative.

## Historical/Mythological Background

The character has roots in older Iranian tradition, appearing in the Avesta-related Kayanian legendary cycle. He is believed to derive from an ancient figure named **Gaēuua** or similar in pre-Islamic Iranian lore, predating Ferdowsi's poetic rendering by many centuries.
